blocks.text: Imagine a world where your code runs faster without changing a single line. Local optimisation techniques like constant folding, common subexpression elimination, and dead code removal make this possible.

blocks.markdown: Local optimisation aims to improve the efficiency of a program by refining its intermediate representation before generating the final machine code. This process involves techniques such as constant folding, common subexpression elimination, and dead code removal. Each of these techniques can significantly enhance the performance of the generated code.

blocks.title: Constant Folding
blocks.text: Constant folding is a compiler optimization technique that simplifies constant expressions at compile time.

blocks.markdown: Consider the expression `3 + 5` in a program. Instead of generating code to perform this addition at runtime, constant folding evaluates it at compile time, replacing it with `8`. This reduces the number of operations the CPU must perform.

blocks.prompt: Apply constant folding to the expression `x = 3 * (2 + 4)`.

steps.text: Replace the original expression with the evaluated result.

blocks.title: Common Subexpression Elimination
blocks.text: Common subexpression elimination (CSE) is an optimization that identifies and eliminates expressions that are computed multiple times.

blocks.markdown: If a program computes `a + b` multiple times, CSE replaces subsequent occurrences with a single variable storing the result of the first computation. This reduces redundant calculations.

blocks.title: Eliminating a Common Subexpression
blocks.prompt: Optimize the code snippet: `c = a + b; d = a + b + c;` using CSE.

steps.text: Introduce a new variable to store the result of the common subexpression.
Replace occurrences of the common subexpression with the new variable.

blocks.answer: The optimized code is: `temp = a + b; c = temp; d = temp + c;`

blocks.title: Dead Code Removal
blocks.text: Dead code removal is the process of eliminating code that does not affect the program's output.

blocks.markdown: Dead code might arise from variables or computations whose results are never used. Removing such code can reduce the size of the program and improve performance.

blocks.title: Identifying Dead Code
blocks.prompt: Identify and remove dead code in the following snippet: `int x = 5; int y = x + 3; int z = 2; return y;`

steps.text: Identify variables whose values are never used.

steps.latex: int x = 5; int y = x + 3; return y;

blocks.answer: The optimized code is: `int x = 5; int y = x + 3; return y;`

blocks.text: Local optimizations can significantly reduce execution time and resource usage by simplifying code before it is compiled into machine language.
